what: Every memory tracer on every page draws its labels below 12px on a phone (median 9.2px, worst 4.5px), because the narrow layout's viewBox is wider than the panel and the SVG is scaled down to fit.
evidence: Measured all 182 [data-tracer] widgets in 142 chapters at 390px, stepping each to its last step; smallest label = 12px class x (rendered width / viewBox width). 182/182 below 12px, 108 below 10px, 28 below 8px. Worst: rust/ch29 tr-pool-box 4.5px, javascript/ch13 tr-trip-box 5.6px, go/ch16 tr-tally-box 5.9px, python/ch12 tr-group-box 5.9px, cpp/ch5 tr-split-box 6.3px. Even the best case is 11.6px: the narrow viewBox floor is 320 (layoutTracer: Math.max(narrow ? 320 : 720, ...)) while the .mem box is about 300px wide. Raw data: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-engine/measure.json (script measure.js).
fix: Draw the narrow layout at natural size and let .mem scroll (it already has overflow-x:auto): in renderTracer after setAttribute('viewBox', ...) add `el.style.width = narrow ? lay.width + 'px' : '';` and in comic-widgets.css change `.tracer-svg.narrow { max-width: 420px; margin: 0 auto; }` to `.tracer-svg.narrow { max-width: none; margin: 0; }`, plus a swipe hint like .mapwrap::before (`.tracer .mem:has(.narrow)::before`). Also lower narrow minimums in objSize (pairs kw 130/vw 144 -> 90/110 when narrow) so most phones need no scroll at all.

what: The tracer diagram zooms in and out between steps: its viewBox width is recomputed from the objects present at each step, so when a wide object appears every label shrinks.
evidence: 131 of 182 tracers change viewBox width while stepping (e.g. go/ch24 tr-wg-box takes 10 different widths, rust/ch29 tr-pool-box 10, go/ch20 tr-stack-box 6). layoutTracer: width = Math.max(..., gutter + (inner + tagArrows) * 12 + 16) where gutter = maxRight + 24 of the objects drawn at this step only; planTracer already fixes slot heights for the whole run but not width.
fix: In mountTracer compute the width once over all steps: `plan.width = {}; [false,true].forEach(function(n){ plan.width[n] = Math.max.apply(null, m.steps.map(function(s,i){ plan.cur = i; return layoutTracer(s, n, plan).width; })); });` and in renderTracer use `Math.max(lay.width, plan.width[narrow])` for the viewBox width (height likewise).

what: Every stack-and-heap stepper ([data-mem]) renders its field labels below their 11px design size on a phone (6.9px to 10.5px), for the same reason as the tracer: width:100% with a viewBox wider than the panel.
evidence: All 35 [data-mem] widgets measured at 390px: smallest mh-lab label 6.9px (rust/ch11 Panel 41), 7.4px (cpp/ch18 Panel 29), 7.6px (rust/ch10 Panel 13), 7.7px (cpp/ch24 Panel 27), 7.8px (rust/ch10 Panel 5); values (16-18px) shrink in proportion. CSS: .mem-svg.narrow { max-width: 460px } with width:100%.
fix: Same change as the tracer: in render() set `svgEl.style.width = narrow ? width + 'px' : '';` and in comic-widgets.css `.mem-svg.narrow { max-width: none; margin: 0; }` (.mem-wrap already scrolls). Raise .mh-lab to 12px.

what: Map labels fall below 12px on phones on every map, because the map keeps min-width 540px for a viewBox that is usually 690 wide.
evidence: 129 maps measured at 390px: smallest rendered text 10.5px to 11.9px, 129/129 below 12px (code tspans .c are 14px x 0.78). Script /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-engine/maps.js, data maps.json.
fix: In the <=640px block add `.map-svg { min-width: 640px; }` (the wrapper already scrolls and shows the swipe hint), or set min-width to the map's own viewBox width from mountMap: `svg.style.minWidth = Math.min(m.size[0], 690) + 'px'`.

what: Rust raw strings with hashes (r#"..."#) are coloured wrongly whenever they contain a quote: the string ends at the first inner quote.
evidence: HL.rust.str = "b?r#*\"[\\s\\S]*?\"#*": the lazy match stops at the first " followed by zero #. Test: highlight('let s = r#"say "hi" now"#;','rust') gives r#"say "hi. Affected real programs shown on pages: rust-ch12/raw.rs (r#"Mabel said "shh" twice"#), rust-ch28/predict_json.rs, serde_errors.rs (6 lines), serde_panic.rs.
fix: Replace the raw-string alternative with explicit hash counts (no backreference, so group numbers stay the same): str: "b?r###\"[\\s\\S]*?\"###|b?r##\"[\\s\\S]*?\"##|b?r#\"[\\s\\S]*?\"#|b?r\"[^\"]*\"|b?" + CSTR + "|b?'(?:\\\\.|[^'\\\\\\n])'".

what: The engine highlighter does not nest Rust block comments, so rs-ch1.js's highlight override is still needed (it is not a redundant workaround).
evidence: highlight(nested_comments.rs,'rust') ends the comment at the inner */ and shows 'still inside the outer one */' as code. rust/ch1 uses nested_comments.rs; rs-ch1.js lines 21-53 replace L.highlight with a nesting scanner.
fix: Port rs-ch1.js chunks() into highlight(): when L2 === 'rust' and src contains '/*', split src into code and nested-comment chunks first, highlight code chunks with the regex and wrap comment chunks in tok-com. Then delete rs-ch1.js's override and rehighlight().

what: Widgets that highlight one line at a time (walker, tracer, spot, parsons) colour a C++ line that starts with '<<' as HTML markup, so its comments, keywords and numbers lose their colours.
evidence: hlLang(): `if (/^\s*</.test(src)) return "html";` runs before the captures' meta.lang. highlight('    << "total: " << n << "\\n"; // done') with meta.lang cpp returns the // comment uncoloured. 42 such lines in cpp programs (cpp-ch27 10, ch11 8, ch16 5, ch9 4, ...).
fix: Only treat text as markup when the page is not a non-JS language and '<' starts a tag: `var m = (captures meta lang); if (/^\s*<(?:[A-Za-z!/])/.test(src) && (!HL[m] || m === 'javascript' || m === 'html')) return 'html';`.

what: 122 terminals marked .term.wrap contain compiler/runtime caret lines under source lines longer than a phone line, so on phones the ^ markers no longer sit under the code they point at (the open 'Terminal wrapping consistency' item, with numbers).
evidence: Scan of every <pre class="term wrap" data-run> against its capture (caret line directly under a line of 36+ characters, cpp-ch18 excluded because its CSS turns wrap off on phones): 131 hits in 38 chapters, e.g. cpp/ch24 12, cpp/ch26 10, cpp/ch8 7, cpp/ch21 6, javascript/ch24 6, javascript/ch28 6, javascript/ch16 5. `.term.wrap { white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` is defined identically in 49 chapter CSS files.
fix: Promote one rule and protect carets: comic.css add `.term.wrap { white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere; } .term.wrap.has-carets { white-space: pre; overflow-wrap: normal; }`; in fillCode after computing segs add `if (/^[ \t]*(?:\d+[ \t]*)?\|?[ \t]*[~\-]*\^[\^~\- ]*(?:[ \t].*)?$/m.test(segs.map(function(s){return s.t;}).join(''))) terms[j].classList.add('has-carets');`. Then delete the 49 chapter copies and the cpp-ch18/rs-ch27 overrides.

what: AUTHORING's model example for visible normalisation is false: javascript ch14 hides its sed exactly like rust ch14 and go ch15 (the terminal prompt shows 'node --test money.test.js'), and capture.py has nothing that stops a hidden output filter.
evidence: AUTHORING: 'normalise it visibly in the shown command, e.g. node --test | sed ..., as js ch14 does'. /home/you/javascript-ch14/money.test.cmd: shown 'node --test money.test.js', real "node --test --test-reporter=spec money.test.js | sed -E 's/ \([0-9.]+ms\)$/ (…ms)/; ...'". 18 such steps in javascript-ch14, 20 in go-ch15; the word 'sed' never appears on javascript/ch14.html (prose only says 'this book shows (…ms)').
fix: capture.py cmd_sidecar() and run_session(): add a problem when the real command pipes into sed/tr/awk/grep/cut but the display text does not: `if re.search(r"\|\s*(sed|tr|awk|grep|cut)\b", real) and not re.search(r"\|\s*(sed|tr|awk|grep|cut)\b", display): problems.append(...)`. Fix the three chapters' display strings to include the pipe, and change AUTHORING's example to one that is true after the fix.

what: The TODO says the C++ '; exit $?' abort workaround is now unnecessary because of ISOLATE_SH, but ISOLATE_SH is only used for plain .cpp builds and Rust .abort; .cmd steps still run 'bash -c CMD' as PID 1, so removing the workaround would break the abort runs.
evidence: cmd_sidecar: `argv = (ISOLATE if (isolate and last) else []) + ["bash", "-c", real]`. bash execs a single simple command directly, so ./at10 becomes PID 1 inside the namespace and ignores SIGABRT. Still relied on by cpp-ch5 at10.cmd, stoi_abc.cmd, stoi_quiz.cmd and cpp-ch6 offby.cmd ('./at10; exit $?'). TODO lines 51 and 53.
fix: Either keep the workaround (and strike the two TODO notes), or make the last .cmd step use ISOLATE_SH for cpp: `argv = (ISOLATE_SH if (isolate and last and cfg_prefix in ('cpp',)) else ISOLATE if (isolate and last) else []) + ['bash','-c', real]` and only then drop '; exit $?'.

what: The slashed-zero setting for code is dead: the later ligature rules set font-feature-settings with !important and replace it rather than adding to it.

fix: Change both ligature rules to `font-feature-settings: "calt" 0, "liga" 0, "zero" 1 !important;` (or delete line 51 if a plain zero is wanted).

what: The fill exercise's 'Your code' column can show the learner's answer in the wrong place: it substitutes the first occurrence of the blank text, ignoring the model's nth, and treats $& / $1 in the typed answer as replacement patterns.
evidence: check(): `mineLines[b.line - 1] = mineLines[b.line - 1].replace(b.text, v || "____");` while the input was placed using b.nth (lines 502-504).
fix: Rebuild the line from the cut positions computed when rendering (store {at,len} per input) and splice: `l.slice(0, at) + v + l.slice(at + len)`, applied right to left; never pass user text as a replacement string.

what: Tracer list/array and object boxes are sized without their header label, so a long `label` (e.g. 'Vec<String> on the heap · v1') can run past the box edge.
evidence: objSize items: `label = (o.kind + "  · ").length * CH.type + 40` ignores o.label and the id; pairs: width = kw + vw + 26 with no label term. The header is drawn as `o.label || (o.kind + "  · " + oid)`.
fix: Use the drawn text: `var head = (o.label || (o.kind + '  · ' + id)).length * CH.type + 24;` and take Math.max with it in both branches (pass id into objSize).

what: Heap block width ignores its label, so a short block with a long label ('#1 · String bytes · FREED') overflows its box.
evidence: heapW(h) = Math.max(170, 16 + n * 34); label drawn at 13px is about 7.8px per character: 25 characters = 195px > 170.
fix: heapW: `Math.max(170, 16 + n * 34, 20 + ("#" + id + " · " + (h.label || "bytes") + " · FREED").length * 7.9)` (pass id).

what: Data files are written with plain write_text although a full disk already emptied a go.mod once; a disk-full during capture leaves a truncated data/<prefix>-chN.js that breaks the page.
evidence: capture(): out_json.write_text(...); out_js.write_text(...). atomic_write() exists in the same file and is only used for go.mod.
fix: Use `if not (atomic_write(out_json, ...) and atomic_write(out_js, ...)): sys.exit('capture: could not write data files')`.

what: A session .cmd with a .stdin sidecar would get a wrong 'screen': the pty rerun executes the placeholder argv ['true'] that run_program returns for session steps.
evidence: run_program session branch returns Step(st[0], ["true"], ...); capture() then runs run_pty(run[-1].argv, ...). No chapter combines them today (checked every */*.cmd with session:true for a .stdin), so this is latent.
fix: In capture(), skip the pty run (or report a problem) when spec.get('session') is true: `if f.with_suffix('.cmd').exists() and json.loads(...).get('session'): problems.append(name + ': .stdin is not supported with session .cmd')`.

what: Browser captures stop 150 ms after the last action, so console output from any later timer, fetch or animation callback is silently missing from the 'real run'.
evidence: await page.waitForTimeout(150) after load and after actions, then browser.close(). Nothing records that the page still had pending timers.
fix: Wait for quiet instead of a fixed time: after actions `await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle'); await page.evaluate(() => new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 300)));` and document the cut-off in the header; authors can still add {"wait": N}.
